archetypes.name: Cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (HE11)
archetypes.summary: Low-loss dielectric puck on a ground plane, radiating in the broadside HE11 mode; resonance and Q fitted to 3-D FDTD ringdowns rather than to the published curve fits.

synthesis.notes: FITTED TO FDTD. ln(sqrt(eps_r)*k0*a) as a polynomial in 1/sqrt(eps_r) and ln(a/h), fitted to 48 ringdowns of the puck on an infinite ground plane (otahub.num.dra.cylinder, at least 16 cells of radius, 8 of height) over eps_r 6-50 and a/h 0.4-4, and NaN outside that: the flat pucks at a/h 5-6 the data keeps as 'outside' sit 1.9% (k0a) and 5.7% (Q) off this fit at eps_r 50 - this note used to say it covered a/h 6. Fit error 0.34% worst, 0.16% on 12 held-out ringdowns. The same solver reproduces the exact hemisphere pole to 0.15%, and refining the grid by half again moves k0*a by 0.1%. Replaces Mongia & Bhartia's published fit, which the ringdowns put from 9.4% low to 8.8% high: 6-9% low on every tall puck (a/h 0.5 and below) whatever the permittivity, and within 3% only for a/h 0.75-4 at eps_r >= 20.

analysis.notes: forward check: must return f0

FITTED TO FDTD: Q = Re/(2 Im) of the same ringdowns, ln(Q/eps_r^1.5) fitted in the same two variables, 0.42% worst on the fitting set and 0.49% held out. The published fit it replaces runs from 26% low to 16% high: 6-26% low at eps_r 12 and below for a/h 0.75-4, where its eps_r^1.3 scaling no longer holds, and up to 16% high on the tallest pucks at high permittivity. It holds to about 3% only for a/h 0.75-2 at eps_r >= 20. NaN outside eps_r 6-50 and a/h 0.4-4, the FDTD training domain.
BW = (S-1)/(Q*sqrt(S)) with S = 2

What Mongia & Bhartia's curve fit, k0*a = (6.324/sqrt(eps_r+2))*(0.27 + 0.36*(a/2h) + 0.02*(a/2h)^2), predicts for THIS puck - the formula the literature sizes pucks with, kept for comparison. 6-9% LOW on tall pucks (a/h <= 0.5) at every permittivity; within 3% for a/h 0.75-4 at eps_r >= 20.
Mongia & Bhartia's Q fit for comparison. Holds to about 3% only for a/h 0.75-2 at eps_r >= 20; 6-26% low at eps_r <= 12, up to 16% high on the tallest pucks.

Derived, not a placeholder: the HE11 mode radiates as a horizontal MAGNETIC dipole, whose image in a perfect ground plane is co-directed rather than reversed. That doubles the free-space 1.5 to exactly 3.0 in the upper half space. Measured DRAs land near 5 dBi, close to this 4.77, with the shortfall from finite ground planes.

validity: resonance and Q are fitted to FDTD over 6 <= eps_r <= 50 and 0.4 <= a/h <= 6; outside that the polynomials extrapolate
isolated resonator: a probe, slot or microstrip feed pulls the resonance by a few percent and is not modelled
no conductor loss and no dielectric loss: real bandwidth is wider and efficiency lower than these figures suggest
HE11 only; the TM01 mode, which radiates like a monopole, and higher modes are not tracked

known_cases.source: FDTD ringdown (otahub.num.dra.cylinder, 20 cells of radius and height) of the default puck at eps_r = 10: k0*a = 0.84100. Mongia & Bhartia's fit gives 0.83064, 1.2% low, which the previous version of this case asserted to 2%.
Same ringdown: Q = 8.633. The published fit gives 7.597, 12% low, overstating the VSWR 2 bandwidth by 14%. The hemisphere's exact pole gives 9.15 at the same permittivity.

eps_r = 20, a/h = 1, 24 cells: k0*a = 0.60902, Q = 19.328, where the published fits hold (0.7% high and 3.2% low). Doubling eps_r from 10 raises Q 2.24 times, not the 2^1.3 = 2.46 the fit's exponent says.
A tall puck, a/h = 0.5, eps_r = 10 (24 cells of height): k0*a = 0.70683. The published fit puts this puck at 9.330 GHz, 6.7% low - it is 6-9% low on every puck this tall.
A flat puck, a/h = 4, eps_r = 10 (12 cells of height, 48 of radius): k0*a = 1.90008, Q = 3.466. The published Q fit gives 2.811, 19% low.
eps_r = 50, a/h = 1, 24 cells: k0*a = 0.39317, Q = 62.83 (published fits 1.5% high and 2.0% low).

references: Mongia & Bhartia, Dielectric Resonator Antennas - A Review, IJMWCAE 4(3), 1994 (the published fits, kept for comparison)
Petosa, Dielectric Resonator Antenna Handbook, Artech House 2007
Resonances and Q computed here by 3-D FDTD ringdown (otahub.num.dra), validated against the exact hemisphere pole, and fitted
Directivity of 3.0 derived from magnetic-dipole image theory; cross-checked against the exact hemispherical solution in this family, which gives the same 3.0

archetypes.name: Hemispherical dielectric resonator antenna
archetypes.summary: Dielectric hemisphere on a ground plane: the one DRA shape with an exact solution, and the reference the others are judged against.

synthesis.notes: Fitted to the EXACT complex natural frequency of the equivalent dielectric sphere's TE1 (magnetic dipole) mode: the root of m*psi1'(m*x)*xi1(x) = xi1'(x)*psi1(m*x) in the complex x = k0*a plane, whose real part is the resonance. Maximum error 0.23% over 6 <= eps_r <= 100. The form carries the right limit: as eps_r grows, sqrt(eps_r)*k0*a -> pi exactly, one internal half wavelength across the diameter, and the correction term is how far short of it a finite permittivity falls. An earlier version took the peak of the Mie scattering coefficient |b1| on the real frequency axis instead, which sits 1.2% high at eps_r = 10: a resonance with Q near 9 is broad enough that the scattering background drags its peak off the pole.

analysis.notes: forward check: must return f0

sqrt(eps_r)*k0*a / pi, which the exact pole puts between 0.929 and 0.983 over 6 <= eps_r <= 50 and which tends to 1 as eps_r grows - the resonance really is 'one internal half wavelength across the diameter', approached from below

Q = Re(x)/(2*Im(x)) at the same complex pole: the ringdown Q, stored energy over energy radiated per radian. Fitted to 0.22% over 6 <= eps_r <= 100 in a form that keeps the magnetic dipole's eps_r^1.5 asymptote. It is NOT a single power law - the best one misses the exact values by 9% somewhere in 8-50. The half-power width of |b1| on the real axis, which the previous version used, UNDERSTATES Q by 12% at eps_r = 10 and 10% at 8, converging on the pole only as Q grows. Mongia & Bhartia's published fit 0.08 + 0.796*eps_r + 0.01226*eps_r^2 - 3e-5*eps_r^3 lands within 1.04% of the pole over 8-50, which says the published fit describes the pole, not the scattering peak. A 3-D FDTD ringdown of a staircased hemisphere (otahub.num.dra) reproduces the pole to 0.9% at eps_r = 10 and 50.
BW = (S-1)/(Q*sqrt(S)) at S = 2
Exactly 3.0, derived: the TE111 mode is a horizontal magnetic dipole, and a magnetic dipole's image in a perfect ground plane is co-directed, so the free-space 1.5 doubles into the upper half space.
hemisphere, so two thirds of the sphere
0.150 at eps_r = 10, falling to 0.070 at eps_r = 50 - the size-versus-bandwidth trade, in one number
Radius in wavelengths times fractional bandwidth. It falls steadily with permittivity, which is the honest summary: high permittivity buys size at a worse-than-linear cost in bandwidth.

validity: 8 <= eps_r <= 50 is the range this family's other fits cover; these two were fitted over 6 to 100 and hold to 0.23% across all of it
infinite perfectly conducting ground plane, which image theory requires
isolated resonator: a probe, slot or microstrip feed perturbs the resonance by a few percent and this spec does not model the feed
lossless dielectric. A real material's tan_d adds an unloaded Q in parallel, widening the bandwidth and lowering the efficiency
TE111 only; higher modes exist and are not tracked

known_cases.source: Exact TE1 pole of the equivalent sphere at eps_r = 10: k0*a = 0.939784 + j0.051356. Solved here by Newton iteration on the characteristic equation in 30-digit arithmetic; the fit gives 0.941671, 0.20% away. The real-axis peak of |b1| that the previous version quoted, 0.95112, is 1.2% higher.

Q = Re/(2 Im) at the same pole: 9.1497. The half-power width of |b1| gives 8.04, 12% low, which is what this case used to assert. otahub.num.dra's FDTD ringdown of a hemisphere 12 cells in radius gives 9.07, and the published Mongia & Bhartia fit 9.24.
eps_r = 20: pole at k0*a = 0.678245, Q = 20.513. Doubling the permittivity from 10 shrinks the radius by 28% and raises Q 2.24 times.
eps_r = 40: k0*a = 0.486663, Q = 49.59, so the VSWR 2 bandwidth has fallen to 1.4%. At this Q the real-axis peak and the pole agree to 0.04% in k0*a and 0.4% in Q: the discrepancy is a low-Q effect.
sqrt(10)*0.939784/pi = 0.94597: the diameter holds a little under one internal half wavelength, and the shortfall shrinks as eps_r grows

references: Leung, Luk, Lai & Lin, Theory and experiment of a coaxial probe fed hemispherical DRA, IEEE T-AP 41(10), 1993
Mongia & Bhartia, Dielectric Resonator Antennas - A Review, IJMWCAE 4(3), 1994
Bohren & Huffman, Absorption and Scattering of Light by Small Particles, Ch. 4 (Mie coefficients)
Complex natural frequencies computed here from the exact characteristic equation and fitted over 6 <= eps_r <= 100; checked against a 3-D FDTD ringdown (otahub.num.dra)

archetypes.name: Rectangular dielectric resonator antenna
archetypes.summary: Dielectric brick on a ground plane in its broadside mode, magnetic dipole along the length; resonance and Q fitted to 3-D FDTD ringdowns rather than taken from the dielectric waveguide model.

parameters.name: width/height ratio w/d (across the magnetic dipole)
length/height ratio L/d (along the magnetic dipole)

synthesis.notes: FITTED TO FDTD. ln(sqrt(eps_r)*k0*d) as a cubic in 1/sqrt(eps_r), ln(L/d) and ln(w/d), fitted to 150 ringdowns of the brick on an infinite ground plane (otahub.num.dra.brick: 12 cells per height, CPML, symmetry planes that admit only the horizontal magnetic dipole) over eps_r 6-50 and both aspect ratios 1-3. Fit error 0.15% worst, 0.13% on 33 held-out ringdowns at other permittivities and aspect ratios. The FDTD reproduces the exact hemisphere pole to 0.15% in frequency and 0.9% in Q, and moves by at most 0.1% (0.2% in Q) when the grid is refined to 16 or 18 cells. Per unit sqrt(eps_r) because that carries nearly all of the permittivity dependence: the brick holds about one internal half wavelength whatever eps_r is.

analysis.notes: forward check from the geometry: must return f0

FITTED TO FDTD: Q = Re/(2 Im) of the same ringdowns' complex frequency, ln(Q/eps_r^1.5) fitted in the same three variables. Worst error 0.68% on the fitting set and 0.65% held out. eps_r^1.5 is the magnetic dipole's high-permittivity scaling, which the hemisphere's exact pole shows. This replaces a Q borrowed from the hemisphere, which was 6% low at the default brick and anywhere from 18% low to 78% high across the design space, because a brick's Q depends on its shape and not only on its permittivity. The dielectric waveguide model's own Q (Mongia & Ittipiboon: stored energy from the DWM fields, radiation from their magnetic moment) is no substitute: 8% low at the default, from 33% low at eps_r = 6 to 26% high at eps_r = 50.
BW = (S-1)/(Q*sqrt(S)) at S = 2

The same brick's OTHER broadside mode, magnetic dipole along w instead of L: the same fit with the two aspect ratios exchanged. Equal to f0 for a square footprint, where the two are degenerate; a feed on the centre of a face couples to one of them and not the other. How far apart they sit is how much room the design has.

Dielectric waveguide model, set up the right way round: the transcendental runs ALONG the magnetic dipole (open faces at each end of L), with magnetic walls across the width and on the top face, whose image doubles the height. (ky^2 + kz^2)*(L/2)^2 with ky = pi/w and kz = pi/(2d).
v = kx*L/2, the root of v*tan(v) = sqrt(((eps_r-1)*P - v^2)/eps_r), fitted in ln P and 1/eps_r to 1.5e-4 over P 0.8-30 and eps_r 6-50. Used only for the comparison below.
The exact DWM condition at the fitted root; it vanishes at the true root. A live check on that fit.

What the dielectric waveguide model predicts for THIS brick. Its error does not shrink with permittivity; it drifts from up to 10.6% HIGH at eps_r = 6 (long narrow bricks) to up to 6.2% LOW at eps_r = 50 (tall ones), and at eps_r = 50 the whole VSWR 2 bandwidth is about 1.2%. The magnetic walls it puts on four faces are an approximation at every permittivity, not a limit that high permittivity approaches.
What an all-magnetic-wall cavity would give: kx = pi/L, ky = pi/w, kz = pi/(2d). It assumes total confinement on every face, so it oversizes the brick.
1.096 for the default brick at eps_r = 10
radius of a sphere of the same volume, for comparing against the hemispherical archetype
Exactly 3.0: a horizontal magnetic dipole whose image in a perfect ground plane is co-directed, doubling the free-space 1.5.

validity: resonance and Q are fitted to FDTD over 6 <= eps_r <= 50 and 1 <= w/d, L/d <= 3; outside that the polynomials extrapolate, and the fit's worst errors quoted in the notes do not apply
the mode designed is the broadside one whose magnetic dipole runs along L. The other one, along w, is reported; higher modes are not tracked
isolated resonator: a probe, slot or microstrip feed pulls the resonance by a few percent and is not modelled
lossless dielectric. A real tan_d adds an unloaded Q in parallel, widening the bandwidth and lowering the efficiency

known_cases.source: FDTD ringdown (otahub.num.dra.brick, 16 cells per height) of the default brick at eps_r = 10: k0*d = 0.78472, d = 3.7441 mm. The dielectric waveguide model gives 3.7325 mm, 0.31% small; this is the one brick where the old and the corrected DWM orientations coincide, because its image is a cube.
Same ringdown: Q = 8.453. The hemisphere's Q, which this spec used to borrow, is 7.96 (6% low); the DWM's own stored-energy Q is 7.754 (8% low).
The DWM condition must vanish at its own root; it nearly does at the fitted one. Expectation of zero, so an absolute tolerance, in its own case.
The all-magnetic-wall cavity gives 4.1051 mm against the ringdown's 3.7441 mm: 9.6% oversize in every dimension, so it predicts the resonance high.
eps_r = 20, default aspect: ringdown k0*d = 0.56845 (d = 2.7123 mm), Q = 18.855. The DWM is already 2.5% low in frequency here.

w = 3d, L = 1.5d, the dipole along the SHORT side: ringdown k0*d = 0.72726, d = 3.4700 mm. The previous spec, solving the transcendental along the height, gave 3.9064 mm - 12.6% too big, because it was describing a vertical magnetic dipole the ground plane shorts out. The same brick's mode along w rings at k0*d = 0.84661, i.e. 11.641 GHz.
Same ringdown: Q = 7.677; the mode along w has 7.290.
The tall corner, a cube standing on the ground at eps_r = 8: ringdown k0*d = 1.40956 (d = 6.7255 mm), Q = 5.193. The old orientation gave 7.7959 mm, 15.9% too big; the borrowed Q was 5.94, 14% high.

eps_r = 50, default aspect, ringdown on an 18-cell grid: k0*d = 0.36709, d = 1.7515 mm. The DWM solved by bisection puts this brick at 9.557 GHz, 4.4% low, while its VSWR 2 bandwidth is only 1.2%: the model the literature sizes bricks with misses the band entirely at high permittivity.

references: Mongia & Ittipiboon, Theoretical and experimental investigations on rectangular DRAs, IEEE T-AP 45(9), 1997 (the dielectric waveguide model and its Q)
Petosa, Dielectric Resonator Antenna Handbook, Artech House 2007, Ch. 3
Resonances and Q computed here by 3-D FDTD ringdown (otahub.num.dra), validated against the exact hemisphere pole, and fitted
